decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0% to 0.25%. The vote was 10-0.

changes.quote: Following sharp declines, economic activity and employment have picked up somewhat in recent months but remain well below their levels at the beginning of the year.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: The virus and the measures taken to protect public health have induced sharp declines in economic activity and a surge in job losses.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: Overall financial conditions have improved in recent months, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Financial conditions have improved, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses.”

changes.quote: The path of the economy will depend significantly on the course of the virus.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

tone_quotes.quote: In light of these developments, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.

To support the flow of credit to households and businesses, over coming months the Federal Reserve will increase its holdings of Treasury securities and agency residential and commercial mortgage-backed securities at least at the current pace to sustain smooth market functioning, thereby fostering effective transmission of monetary policy to broader financial conditions.
The coronavirus outbreak is causing tremendous human and economic hardship across the United States and around the world.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 15.09% APR costs about $62.88 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 0.58% and moved -1 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 2.98% would fall by about $1.62 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 11%, and employers added an average of -4,408k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 0.7% over the past year (June 2020); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a -28% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -2 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 1.24%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.09% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 22%, cut 78%, hike 0%.
